h: Painted Halls, Dolls' Houses and Dragon Heads
p: Wallington was home to the Trevelyan family, a lively bunch of thinkers, writers and campaigners who gave the estate to the National Trust in the 1940s. Inside, the Central Hall is the star: its walls are painted with scenes from Northumberland's history by William Bell Scott, a friend of the Pre-Raphaelites, from Roman soldiers on Hadrian's Wall to Tyneside industry. It's a brilliant way to get a sense of the county's story in one room.

There's plenty to tickle younger visitors too. Look out for the collection of dolls' houses and the cabinet of curiosities stuffed with odd objects. Outside, on the lawn, a row of stone dragon or griffin heads stares out across the grass. They're said to have come from one of London's old city gates, brought north as ballast on a ship, and they make a fabulous photo spot.
Here's another fun fact: Capability Brown was born just down the road at Kirkharle and went to school in the estate village of Cambo. You can almost picture him learning about landscapes right here.

Allow most of a day if you want to see the house, garden and estate walks. Cambo is a pretty little village worth a quick look, and Kirkharle Courtyard nearby has craft shops and a café. Morpeth itself has the Chantry Bagpipe Museum, celebrating the Northumbrian smallpipes, and Carlisle Park by the River Wansbeck for a gentle evening stroll.
